description: The Maharashtra government will introduce digital autopsy facilities at KEM and JJ hospitals in Mumbai, enabling non-invasive, AI-based postmortem examinations. The initiative aims to improve accuracy, reduce delays, support investigations, and address sensitivities of grieving families, with plans to expand statewide.
body_lead: Mumbai, Dec 27: In a significant step toward modernising forensic medicine, the Maharashtra government has decided to introduce digital autopsy facilities in government hospitals on a phased basis. The initiative will begin with KEM Hospital and JJ Hospital in Mumbai, where postmortem examinations will be conducted without traditional incisions, using artificial intelligence–based imaging technology.
